source_capture_policy.admission_rule: Do not use as a model feature until byte-complete SEC filing captures and SHA-256 receipts are stored with independent capture timestamps. Financial facts may be used for human research with the cited filing context.

source_registry.rendered_excerpt: SEC 424B3 dated 2026-10-30: up to 5,218,935 Class A shares may be issued and sold by Evernorth to CF Principal Investments LLC (Cantor) at Evernorth's sole discretion. The cover states potential gross proceeds up to approximately $76.8 million and a $521,893.50 upfront commitment fee. The offering summary Use of Proceeds line states $80.7 million. The Use of Proceeds section states up to $76.8 million gross and up to $74.4 million estimated net over approximately 14 months after estimated fees and expenses. The purchase price is 97% of VWAP. The company may sell all, some or none. Cantor may resell all, some or none. If all 5,218,935 shares were issued, they would be 16.7% of post-issuance Class A shares. At $14.71, the table reports $76.8 million, while its footnote says purchase price equals 97% of assumed trading price. $5,218,935 x $14.71 = $76,770,533.85; multiplied by 97% = $74,467,417.83. The table and other summary figures are not fully arithmetically reconciled.

SEC 8-K dated 2026-10-23: Evernorth may, at its option, sell up to 5,218,935 newly issued Class A shares to Cantor, subject to conditions. Purchase price is 97% of VWAP. Purchases are constrained by Cantor's 4.99% beneficial-ownership cap and 20% of trading volume, with a threshold price. Evernorth owes a $521,893.50 upfront commitment fee after the registration statement becomes effective; the fee is fully earned and non-refundable regardless of purchases, with aggregate commitment fees capped at $1 million. Expense reimbursements are separately capped at $500,000.
SEC EFFECT filing accession 9999999995-26-003391: Evernorth registration statement file 333-299620 had an effectiveness date of 2026-10-30; the notice was accepted 2026-11-02 00:15:10 UTC.

SEC filing disclosure: Advance Funding investors contributed $214,049,995 cash by 2025-10-23 and 600,000 XRP by 2025-10-24; Evernorth used the cash to purchase 84,365,876 XRP. Separately, at the 2026-10-09 business-combination closing, Evernorth issued $30.0 million aggregate principal amount of convertible notes and received $29.0 million net cash proceeds after a $1.0 million fee.

arithmetic_reconciliation.discrepancy: The prospectus's offering summary states $80.7M; its cover/use-of-proceeds states $76.8M; its net estimate is $74.4M; the illustrative table shows $76.8M at $14.71 while the footnote says 97% of trading price. The 97%-adjusted calculation is about $74.47M before expenses. Do not silently reconcile these figures.

eloc_facility.fee_due: within five business days after the registration statement becomes effective
eloc_facility.fee_character: non-refundable and fully earned regardless of whether purchases are made or settled

key_distinctions: Facility capacity is not cash received.
Cantor's later resale proceeds belong to Cantor; Evernorth's proceeds arise from its optional primary share sales to Cantor.
The ELOC's registration effectiveness makes the facility available subject to conditions; it does not prove that any shares have been sold or any proceeds received.
A commitment fee is a financing cost, not capital raised.
Prior cash subscriptions and in-kind XRP contributions must not be counted as current ELOC proceeds.
An issuer statement that proceeds may be used to acquire XRP is an intended use, not evidence of an executed XRP purchase.
Evernorth identifies BitGo, not Coinbase, as its XRP custodian; Coinbase is its principal market reference for fair-value measurement in the reviewed prospectus.
SBI Holdings is the parent identified in Evernorth's cap table; the named controlled investment entities are distinct from regional SBIC East/Central/West companies.
The 39.9% SBI and 9.9% Ripple limits are ownership caps, not independently verified exact current ownership percentages.
Ripple's $9.7M related-party credit draw is debt and became repayable after the October 9 closing; repayment status is not established here.
competing_hypotheses: If Evernorth draws the facility and directs net proceeds into XRP, it could create an incremental institutional purchase channel; the actual timing and size depend on issuer notices, market price, volume limits and the use of proceeds.
Evernorth may draw little or none of the facility if market conditions, share price, dilution costs or alternative financing make it unattractive.
Even if the facility is drawn, the resulting XRP acquisition could be executed over time or through counterparties and may not be visible as a single exchange purchase.
The financing can affect XRPN equity supply and dilution independently of any direct XRP market purchase.
disconfirming_evidence: No ELOC draw amount or settled proceeds were established in the reviewed filings.
The issuer is obligated to pay a non-refundable commitment fee even if no purchases are made.
The purchase price is discounted to VWAP and subject to volume, ownership and threshold-price limits.
The prospectus contains conflicting gross/net proceeds figures and an arithmetic inconsistency that must be preserved.
The historical $214.05M cash subscription and $29M net note proceeds are separate from the ELOC and must not be double-counted.
next_required_work: Monitor subsequent SEC filings and issuer disclosures for actual ELOC purchase notices, share issuance, fees paid and proceeds received.
Reconcile the prospectus proceeds table with the 97% VWAP purchase formula and expense assumptions.
Track any proceeds-to-XRP purchases separately from XRPN share issuance and secondary-market resales.
Capture original SEC filing bytes and hash them before any feature-store admission.
